title: Reserve Fleet Tempo Dashboard and Burst Orchestrator — compact UX prototype
creator: Liam Chen
description: Design a compact operational dashboard and control surface for Dedicated GPU fleets that surfaces pool health, cost projection, autoscaling intent, and an editable burst orchestrator. The goal is to give platform engineers and SREs a concise single-panel view for triage and burst management while preserving safe defaults and guardrails. This ticket covers exploratory sketches, a high-fidelity Figma prototype (desktop + narrow tablet), an interactive burst composer, and a readiness checklist for handoff to web/frontend engineering.
acceptance_criteria: A focused dashboard tile shows 3-minute latency P95, request QPS, GPU utilization, and pre-warmed instance count with color-coded health state
An inline burst orchestrator allows specifying: burst target GPUs, duration, budget cap, and automated rollback on error
Cost projection widget estimates incremental spend for the configured burst and shows per-token and per-hour breakdown
Autoscale policy editor supports hysteresis (min/max), scale step, and schedule overrides with clear preview of expected capacity curve
Design includes accessibility text alternatives, keyboard-first controls for the burst composer, and colorblind-friendly palettes
Figma prototype links, component spec, and a handoff checklist (tokens, API surface, telemetry event list) are attached
comments: 2026-03-01 Liam Chen: Kickoff — aligned with PM Marco Ruiz and Eng lead Priya Nair. PM asks for cost-first view for finance-conscious teams; Eng requests lightweight telemetry queries to avoid expensive dashboard calls.

2026-03-03 Asha Kapoor: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma. Two approaches explored: 'timeline-first' and 'knobboard'. Decided to merge the timeline sparklines with an inline knob composer to keep vertical space low.

2026-03-04 Marco Ruiz (PM): Feedback — add explicit rollback/abort button and a graduated safety confirmation for bursts that exceed budget. Also request sample API payloads for the orchestrator to validate with backend.

2026-03-06 Priya Nair (Eng): Review — backend telemetry team prefers a single paginated query for 1s-sampled metrics; suggested downsampling for P95 to 1m buckets. Asked to annotate which metrics are live vs derived.

2026-03-07 Asha Kapoor: Updated prototype applied. Introduced cost projection microchart and 'safe-mode' toggle for default bursts. Created interaction spec for keyboard accessibility and microcopy for confirmations.
2026-03-08 Design review: Decision to show 'expected latency delta' when enabling burst to avoid surprising regressions. Trade-off: slightly more cognitive load vs clearer reliability signal.
2026-03-09 Engineering handoff prep: Added telemetry event list and proposed REST payloads. Action: ENG to confirm API names by 2026-03-12 (ENG-7829).
2026-03-10 Marco Ruiz (PM): Approves prototype for scheduled usability testing with two internal SREs and one external beta customer. Follow-up: capture feedback and update copy for error states.
notes: Implementation note: autoscale preview uses server-side simulation endpoint (ENG-7831). If unavailable, use client-side estimate to avoid blocking UI rollout.
Accessibility: all interactive controls must be reachable via tab and have aria-labels matching microcopy in the component spec.
Telemetry: emit events 'burst_initiated', 'burst_aborted', 'burst_completed', and 'burst_rollforward' with burst_id and user_id metadata.
